preamble.summary: Psalm 62 (MT) / Psalm 61 (LXX) is a Davidic meditation of silent-trust-in-God alone. The Hebrew adverb 'ak ('only, alone, surely') opens six of the psalm's verses (2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10), signaling the exclusivity-of-divine-reliance as the psalm's theological-center. Verse 12 — 'you, O LORD, belong steadfast love; you will render to each according to his work' — is cited or echoed at Matthew 16:27 ('the Son of Man … will render to each according to his deeds') and Romans 2:6.
preamble.notable_variants: 62:1–2, 5 'for God alone my soul waits in silence' as contemplative-signature; 62:12 'render to each according to his work' → Matt 16:27 / Rom 2:6 / 2 Tim 4:14 / Rev 22:12 retribution-by-deeds principle.
preamble.structural_notes: MT Ps 62 = LXX Ps 61. 13 verses (MT/LXX), 12 verses (English). Dedicated to Jeduthun (cf. Pss 39, 77).

variant_notes: Superscription 'to the choirmaster, to Jeduthun, a Psalm of David' tracks MT.

'For God alone my soul waits in silence; from him comes my salvation' tracks MT. SILENCE-BEFORE-GOD contemplative-theology. The 'alone' (ak) as exclusivity-marker. Lamentations 3:26 ('it is good that one should wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD') extends.
'He only is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be greatly shaken' tracks MT.
'How long will all of you attack a man?' tracks MT. 'Leaning wall / tottering fence' — fragile-human-state imagery.
'They only plan to thrust him down from his high position' tracks MT.
'For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him' tracks MT. Self-addressing-soul imperative — Augustinian contemplative-pattern.
'He only is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be shaken' tracks MT — REFRAIN varied from v. 3 ('not greatly shaken' → 'not shaken' absolute).
'On God rests my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is God' tracks MT.

'Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us' tracks MT. POUR-OUT-YOUR-HEART pastoral-psychological theology. 1 Peter 5:7 and Hebrews 4:16 develop open-access-to-God theology.

'Those of low estate are but a breath; those of high estate are a delusion; in the balances they go up; they are together lighter than a breath' tracks MT. BREATH-AND-BALANCE imagery — human-weightlessness theology recurring at Psalms 144:4, Eccl 1:2 et al.

'Put no trust in extortion; set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, set not your heart on them' tracks MT. 1 Timothy 6:17 ('charge those who are rich in this present age not to be haughty, nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches') parallels the anti-riches-trust pastoral.
'Once God has spoken; twice have I heard this: that power belongs to God' tracks MT. ONCE-TWICE WISDOM FORMULA (proverbial device — cf. Job 33:14, 40:5). Power-belongs-to-God monotheistic axiom.

verses.mt_reading: וּלְךָ־אֲדֹנָי חָסֶד כִּי־אַתָּה תְשַׁלֵּם לְאִישׁ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ
verses.lxx_reading: καὶ σοῦ κύριε τὸ ἔλεος ὅτι σὺ ἀποδώσεις ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ
verses.mt_rendering: And to you, O Lord, belongs steadfast love; for you render to each according to his work
verses.variant_rendering: And to you, O Lord, belongs mercy; for you will render to each according to his works
variant_notes: RETRIBUTION-BY-WORKS PRINCIPLE. This verse — 'render to each according to his works' (apodōseis hekastō kata ta erga autou) — is the LXX-source for a widely-cited NT retribution-by-deeds formula: (a) Matthew 16:27 ('the Son of Man … will render to each person according to his deeds'); (b) Romans 2:6 ('who will render to each one according to his works'); (c) 2 Timothy 4:14 ('the Lord will repay him according to his deeds'); (d) Revelation 2:23, 20:12, 22:12 ('I am coming soon, bringing my recompense with me, to repay everyone for what he has done'). The Davidic-axiom becomes the NT's standard eschatological-judgment formula.

The pairing of 'MERCY (chesed / eleos) AND RETRIBUTION' in one verse is theologically significant: the same God who shows chesed also judges-by-works. The two are not in tension but fused in divine-character.
